scope: Group B final splits and the slip-42 occlusion question.

material_finding.title: Annotations outside the bank memo box are owner-typed supplements, not third-party marks
material_finding.owner_statement: Bangkok Bank imposes a length limit on the transfer note, so the owner types the item breakdown onto the screenshot himself.
why_this_matters: It establishes the PROVENANCE of every annotation found outside a memo box in this batch (slips 42, 48, 97, 110 and others). They are the owner's own contemporaneous record of what a payment covered, not unattributed writing.

It explains why the richest item detail in this batch sits outside the bank memo field rather than inside it — and confirms that any parser reading only the bank memo would systematically lose the itemisation on Bangkok Bank payments.
It resolves the slip-42 occlusion question: the annotation is complete as authored, so no hidden fifth line exists.

Annotation provenance is now 'owner_authored_supplement'. This is stronger evidence than an anonymous mark, but it is still a self-reported breakdown rather than a supplier document — recorded as such.

capitalisation_treatment.basis: Consistent with the owner's explicit instruction to book 'other equipment ฿1,721' (slip 102) to OPEX, and with the owner directing per-branch allocation of these items without directing capitalisation.
capitalisation_treatment.effect: Cameras, tables, cutting boards and shop fit-out are charged in full to August rather than capitalised and spread. This reduces August profit for B1/B2/B3 relative to a capitalisation treatment. Recorded here so the basis is visible and correctable.
